BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every liability and completion point. Taken together, the changes would:

- shrink our recovery through a lower cap, a higher basket and a shorter claims period;
- pull Title and Fundamental claims into the general regime;
- remove our fraud protection;
- let the Seller disclose against the whole data room;
- leave three known completion risks (Bluefen, Riverlark and the bonuses) unresolved or quietly priced against us.

None of these positions should be accepted as drafted.

---

## Preliminary point: the "FINAL / settled at principal level" framing

The preamble says the positions "were settled at principal level by both deal teams," are "FINAL" and are "not intended to be re-opened." It also says 10–20% caps, 1% baskets and 12–18 month periods are "standard market."

- **This is the Seller's assertion, not ours.** We have no written authority from Amelia Frost approving the 20% cap or the 18-month period for this draft. Our playbook makes both fallbacks conditional on that written authority. Without it, our starting positions stand. A statement in the counterparty's cover note cannot satisfy that condition.
- **"Market" arguments are advocacy.** They do not change our mandate.
- **Recommended action:** Before responding, confirm directly with Amelia Frost whether she discussed any of these terms with Harbourglass. If she did, we would need her written authority identifying SPA-003 before using any fallback. Either way, our mark-up should state plainly that nothing is agreed until it is documented in the SPA.

---

## A. Liability regime

### 1. General cap (cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m
**Departure.** Our position is 25% / AUD 6.0m. The AUD 4.8m figure is our conditional fallback, and it is not available without Amelia Frost's written authority. **Push back to 25% / AUD 6.0m.**

### 2. Thresholds (cl 12.2): AUD 25k de minimis, AUD 250k basket, excess only
This is a material departure on three levels:
- The de minimis is 5x ours (AUD 5k).
- The basket is 5x ours (AUD 50k).
- It is a **deductible**, not a tipping basket. Our position is that the Seller is liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.

**Effect:** The first AUD 250k of valid loss is permanently absorbed by us. Any claim under AUD 25k is excluded, so related small claims could disappear entirely unless they are aggregated. **Reject. Revert to AUD 5k / AUD 50k on a tipping basis.** We should also add an aggregation rule so that claims arising from the same or related facts count as one claim for the de minimis.

### 3. Claims period (cl 12.3): 18 months
**Departure.** Our position is 24 months. The 18-month period is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. **Revert to 24 months.**

### 4. "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13)
**This is a hidden general-regime override and it is a serious problem.** It reverses the default. Every Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnity, payment-obligation and covenant claim would become subject to the general cap, thresholds and 18-month period unless we catch and expressly carve out each one. **Delete.** The drafting should do the opposite: general limitations apply *only* to general Warranty Claims, and each other category has its own expressly stated regime.

### 5. Fundamental / Title folded into the general regime
**This is a direct conflict with our playbook.** "Administrative simplicity" does not justify capping our recovery for title and capacity at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m purchase. If title fails, we lose the whole asset. **Reject.** We require a separate regime with:
- a 100% cap (AUD 24m);
- a claims period of at least six years;
- exclusion from the general basket, the de minimis and any knowledge bar.

### 6. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
**This is the most serious issue in the package.** There is no fraud carve-out. On its face, the drafting would cap, time-bar and channel into the exclusive remedy even claims for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct. The non-reliance clause would also be used against misrepresentation claims.

**Reject, with no fallback.** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. Our playbook says no one may waive this, including principals. Even if the Seller later claims a principal-level agreement on this point, it would not change our position.

### 7. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
**Departure.** Tax and IP are **open** items. We have not agreed to fold them into the general regime. Equally, we should not suggest that unlimited liability has been agreed. **Response:** Record them as open in the issues list, keep them as separate categories in the drafting, and negotiate them on their own terms.

---

## B. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

### 8. General disclosure (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **1.1** discloses everything "contained or referred to" in the entire data room.
- **1.2** discloses the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."

This is the whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure that our playbook rejects. The words "referred to" go even further: they would deem disclosed any document that is merely mentioned in a data room document, even if we never received it. **Delete 1.1 and 1.2.** Disclosure should be specific and fair only, meaning it identifies the fact, matter and warranty with enough detail for us to assess its nature and scope.

The data-room cut-off is also **22 September 2026**, which is about six weeks ago. We should require an updated, specific disclosure at signing and a bring-down regime that allows us to terminate or claim if new matters arise between signing and Completion.

### 9. Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3)
This is a blanket bar covering anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, or that was "discoverable from the data room or public records." It is effectively a second layer of deemed disclosure. Combined with the general disclosure clauses, it would also cancel the specific protections we are negotiating. For example, we plainly know about Ironquay, DD-006 and Bluefen. On the Seller's drafting, that knowledge alone could defeat our indemnities for those very matters.

**Delete.** If any knowledge qualifier survives, it must:
- apply to Seller knowledge only, limited to named Seller knowledge persons and qualified by reasonable enquiry;
- never apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### 10. Non-admission (Disclosure Letter 1.4)
This is broadly acceptable as a statement that disclosure does not admit liability. However, we should add a provision that 1.4, and the disclosure generally, cannot qualify or reduce any specific indemnity, Completion deliverable or condition.

---

## C. Completion mechanics and known risks

### 11. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3): reasonable endeavours, satisfied "on delivery"
**Why this is material:** Bluefen generates about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30% of the business. DD-002 contains a change-control consent requirement (cl 11.2) with conditions (cl 11.3). The Seller's own Disclosure Letter (item 2) confirms there is **no final written consent and no evidence that the conditions are satisfied.**

The Seller's drafting fails on both of our requirements:
- Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- "Satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" means a consent that is itself conditional, or whose 11.3 conditions remain unmet, would still satisfy the condition. We could then be compelled to complete into a live termination risk on 30% of revenue.

**Push back.** Make it a condition precedent that:
- an effective, unconditional Bluefen consent is obtained;
- the Seller provides evidence satisfactory to us that each cl 11.3 condition is satisfied, before Completion;
- the Seller is subject to a stronger efforts obligation (all reasonable steps, with Buyer consultation and approval of the consent form);
- we have a right to walk if the condition is not met by the sunset date.

### 12. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): release "following Completion"
**Why this is material:** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding under DD-003. It contains a change-control clause (8.1) and a discharge clause (9.2). The Seller confirms (item 3) that the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included. A change of control without prior repayment may trigger the 8.1 event of default against the company we are buying. A post-completion release leaves the security over our new asset in place.

This is also a debt-free/cash-free deal, so the facility must come out of the price.

**Push back.** At Completion we require:
- a current payout letter from Riverlark;
- direct repayment from Completion funds, shown as a funds-flow line;
- effective, signed releases of all security, including deeds of release, PPSR discharges and the return of any title documents.

A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists at present.

### 13. DD-005 bonuses: "a matter for the Seller" but not itemised
**This is a silent cost shift.** DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000. They are payable by the Company, are triggered by Completion, and the Disclosure Letter (item 5) confirms they are not in the funds flow. Calling them "a matter for the Seller" is meaningless if nothing in the price mechanics makes the Seller bear them. As drafted, the Company pays them after Completion, so we bear the cost. Payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are also unaddressed and sit on top of the AUD 420k.

**Push back.** The AUD 420k, together with all triggered on-costs, must either be a specific funds-flow line deducted from the price (as Debt or a transaction expense) or be funded by the Seller at Completion. We should add a specific indemnity for any shortfall, including on-costs that are determined later.

### 14. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1): indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment
Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. Until the fees are paid, Ironquay may retain the IP in materials the business relies on. An indemnity limited to the payment does not cover the consequences, such as:
- infringement exposure;
- the cost of re-work or replacement;
- customer claims;
- a dispute about whether all fees were in fact paid.

**Push back.** Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or to hold a sufficient licence to, the SOW3 Project Materials. We should **preserve the cure**: payment of the outstanding SOW3 fees combined with a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay. Ideally that cure is delivered at or before Completion, or the AUD 180k is retained or escrowed until it is.

**Caution on the figure:** The AUD 180k is not independently verified. We should not assume it is owed or that it has been paid. We should ask for bank evidence or an Ironquay statement of account.

### 15. DD-006 export/privacy incident: "not expected to be material"
The Seller's characterisation is unsupported. Its own Disclosure Letter (item 6) says the material does not establish whether anyone accessed the file, what the exact scope is, or whether notification is required. Our position must be equally disciplined in the other direction: **we should not assert a confirmed breach, harm, a notification duty or any loss figure.**

**Push back.** Reject the "not material" framing, which may later be used to argue that a warranty is satisfied. Instead require:
- preservation of all relevant logs and evidence;
- a proper investigation with an agreed scope;
- regular written updates to us before Completion;
- a covenant that no notification decision or regulator or customer communication is made without consulting us.

The broader specific protection for this matter can be held for the indemnity discussion once the investigation produces facts.

### 16. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k): "ordinary-course operating costs"
DD-008 and DD-011 show three related renewals of AUD 110k each. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course. The Seller's label is not evidence. Equally, our playbook does not allow us to classify them automatically as Debt or to deduct them from the price.

**Response:** Ask for the contracts and for details of timing, terminability, accrual treatment and the relationship between the three renewals. We should reserve our position on treatment pending that assessment.

### 17. Title evidenced by the DD-012 register
The DD-012 register is the Seller's internal record. Item 10 of the Disclosure Letter expressly avoids saying it has been verified. It is a supplied source, not independent proof.

**Require independent evidence of:**
- **ownership:** a current ASIC company extract consistent with the register, original or replacement share certificates, and the share issue and transfer history;
- **no encumbrances:** a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company, plus Seller confirmation;
- **authority:** a Seller board resolution approving the sale, the constitution, and any shareholder agreement with pre-emption waivers.

We use ASIC and PPSR searches as *our* verification tools. That is distinct from, and does not concede, the Seller's attempt to treat public registers as deemed disclosure.

### 18. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
These are lower risk on the face of the disclosure. The lease requires notification only, and the Mossvale restriction is an assignment restriction that is not triggered by a share sale. **Action:** Verify both against the underlying documents. Add a covenant that the Seller procures the lease notification within the required time. Make sure the general disclosure does not convert these items into accepted risks if the documents turn out to say otherwise.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m.** No fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority. |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k, excess only | **AUD 5k / AUD 50k, first-dollar tipping basket**, plus an aggregation rule |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months | **24 months.** No fallback without written approval. |
| 4 | "Limitations apply to all Claims" | Default override | **Delete.** General limits apply only to general Warranty Claims. |
| 5 | Title/Fundamental | General regime | **Separate regime:** 100% cap, 6+ years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar |
| 6 | Fraud | No carve-out | **Full carve-out from everything. Non-negotiable.** |
| 7 | Tax/IP | "Settled" | **Open.** Separate categories. No resolution assumed. |
| 8 | Disclosure | Whole data room plus public records | **Specific fair disclosure only.** Updated letter and bring-down. |
| 9 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, including "discoverable" | **Delete.** Any qualifier limited to named Seller persons with reasonable enquiry, never for title, capacity, fraud or indemnities. |
| 10 | Bluefen (30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours, consent on delivery | **CP:** effective consent plus evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are met before Completion, with stronger efforts |
| 11 | Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m) | Post-completion release | **Payout letter, direct repayment from funds, releases at Completion** |
| 12 | Bonuses (AUD 420k plus on-costs) | Off the funds flow | **Funds-flow line item or Seller-funded,** plus an indemnity |
| 13 | Ironquay | Payment-only indemnity | **Broaden to ownership/IP loss.** Preserve the payment plus confirmatory assignment cure. Verify the AUD 180k. |
| 14 | DD-006 | "Not material" | **Reject that label.** Preserve logs, investigate, provide updates, consult us. No breach or loss assumed. |
| 15 | Sandbar (AUD 330k) | Ordinary course | **Request documents and assess.** Reserve treatment. No automatic Debt classification. |
| 16 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent evidence:** ASIC, certificates, PPSR, authority documents |
| 17 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification only | Verify the documents. Add a notification covenant. |

**Priority order for the mark-up:**
1. Fraud carve-out
2. Title/Fundamental regime, including deleting the "all Claims" override
3. Bluefen condition precedent
4. Riverlark payout at Completion
5. Bonus funds flow
6. Disclosure and buyer knowledge
7. Cap, thresholds and claims period
8. Ironquay, DD-006 and Sandbar
9. Tax and IP, kept open

**Immediate next step:** Confirm with Amelia Frost whether any principal-level discussion took place. If any fallback is to be used, obtain her written authority referencing SPA-003. Then issue our mark-up with a cover note stating that no term is agreed or final until it is documented in an executed SPA.

The data-room cut-off is also **22 September 2026**, which is about six weeks ago. We should require an updated, specific disclosure at signing and a bring-down regime that allows us to terminate or claim if new matters arise between signing and Completion.

### 9. Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3)
This is a blanket bar covering anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, or that was "discoverable from the data room or public records." It is effectively a second layer of deemed disclosure. Combined with the general disclosure clauses, it would also cancel the specific protections we are negotiating. For example, we plainly know about Ironquay, DD-006 and Bluefen. On the Seller's drafting, that knowledge alone could defeat our indemnities for those very matters.

**Delete.** If any knowledge qualifier survives, it must:
- apply to Seller knowledge only, limited to named Seller knowledge persons and qualified by reasonable enquiry;
- never apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### 10. Non-admission (Disclosure Letter 1.4)
This is broadly acceptable as a statement that disclosure does not admit liability. However, we should add a provision that 1.4, and the disclosure generally, cannot qualify or reduce any specific indemnity, Completion deliverable or condition.

## C. Completion mechanics and known risks

### 11. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3): reasonable endeavours, satisfied "on delivery"
**Why this is material:** Bluefen generates about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30% of the business. DD-002 contains a change-control consent requirement (cl 11.2) with conditions (cl 11.3). The Seller's own Disclosure Letter (item 2) confirms there is **no final written consent and no evidence that the conditions are satisfied.**

The Seller's drafting fails on both of our requirements:
- Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- "Satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" means a consent that is itself conditional, or whose 11.3 conditions remain unmet, would still satisfy the condition. We could then be compelled to complete into a live termination risk on 30% of revenue.

**Push back.** Make it a condition precedent that:
- an effective, unconditional Bluefen consent is obtained;
- the Seller provides evidence satisfactory to us that each cl 11.3 condition is satisfied, before Completion;
- the Seller is subject to a stronger efforts obligation (all reasonable steps, with Buyer consultation and approval of the consent form);
- we have a right to walk if the condition is not met by the sunset date.

### 12. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): release "following Completion"
**Why this is material:** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding under DD-003. It contains a change-control clause (8.1) and a discharge clause (9.2). The Seller confirms (item 3) that the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included. A change of control without prior repayment may trigger the 8.1 event of default against the company we are buying. A post-completion release leaves the security over our new asset in place.

This is also a debt-free/cash-free deal, so the facility must come out of the price.

**Push back.** At Completion we require:
- a current payout letter from Riverlark;
- direct repayment from Completion funds, shown as a funds-flow line;
- effective, signed releases of all security, including deeds of release, PPSR discharges and the return of any title documents.

A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists at present.

### 13. DD-005 bonuses: "a matter for the Seller" but not itemised
**This is a silent cost shift.** DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000. They are payable by the Company, are triggered by Completion, and the Disclosure Letter (item 5) confirms they are not in the funds flow. Calling them "a matter for the Seller" is meaningless if nothing in the price mechanics makes the Seller bear them. As drafted, the Company pays them after Completion, so we bear the cost. Payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are also unaddressed and sit on top of the AUD 420k.

**Push back.** The AUD 420k, together with all triggered on-costs, must either be a specific funds-flow line deducted from the price (as Debt or a transaction expense) or be funded by the Seller at Completion. We should add a specific indemnity for any shortfall, including on-costs that are determined later.

### 14. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1): indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment
Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. Until the fees are paid, Ironquay may retain the IP in materials the business relies on. An indemnity limited to the payment does not cover the consequences, such as:
- infringement exposure;
- the cost of re-work or replacement;
- customer claims;
- a dispute about whether all fees were in fact paid.

**Push back.** Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or to hold a sufficient licence to, the SOW3 Project Materials. We should **preserve the cure**: payment of the outstanding SOW3 fees combined with a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay. Ideally that cure is delivered at or before Completion, or the AUD 180k is retained or escrowed until it is.

**Caution on the figure:** The AUD 180k is not independently verified. We should not assume it is owed or that it has been paid. We should ask for bank evidence or an Ironquay statement of account.

### 15. DD-006 export/privacy incident: "not expected to be material"
The Seller's characterisation is unsupported. Its own Disclosure Letter (item 6) says the material does not establish whether anyone accessed the file, what the exact scope is, or whether notification is required. Our position must be equally disciplined in the other direction: **we should not assert a confirmed breach, harm, a notification duty or any loss figure.**

**Push back.** Reject the "not material" framing, which may later be used to argue that a warranty is satisfied. Instead require:
- preservation of all relevant logs and evidence;
- a proper investigation with an agreed scope;
- regular written updates to us before Completion;
- a covenant that no notification decision or regulator or customer communication is made without consulting us.

The broader specific protection for this matter can be held for the indemnity discussion once the investigation produces facts.

### 16. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k): "ordinary-course operating costs"
DD-008 and DD-011 show three related renewals of AUD 110k each. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course. The Seller's label is not evidence. Equally, our playbook does not allow us to classify them automatically as Debt or to deduct them from the price.

**Response:** Ask for the contracts and for details of timing, terminability, accrual treatment and the relationship between the three renewals. We should reserve our position on treatment pending that assessment.

### 17. Title evidenced by the DD-012 register
The DD-012 register is the Seller's internal record. Item 10 of the Disclosure Letter expressly avoids saying it has been verified. It is a supplied source, not independent proof.

**Require independent evidence of:**
- **ownership:** a current ASIC company extract consistent with the register, original or replacement share certificates, and the share issue and transfer history;
- **no encumbrances:** a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company, plus Seller confirmation;
- **authority:** a Seller board resolution approving the sale, the constitution, and any shareholder agreement with pre-emption waivers.

We use ASIC and PPSR searches as *our* verification tools. That is distinct from, and does not concede, the Seller's attempt to treat public registers as deemed disclosure.

### 18. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
These are lower risk on the face of the disclosure. The lease requires notification only, and the Mossvale restriction is an assignment restriction that is not triggered by a share sale. **Action:** Verify both against the underlying documents. Add a covenant that the Seller procures the lease notification within the required time. Make sure the general disclosure does not convert these items into accepted risks if the documents turn out to say otherwise.
